claims.text: Inducing serrated grain boundaries by post-fabrication heat treatment enhances creep resistance in an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating.
The as-fabricated coating has a primarily FCC matrix.
The as-fabricated coating contains uniformly dispersed L12 precipitates.
The untreated baseline has straight, non-serrated grain boundaries.
Reducing the cooling rate during solution heat treatment promotes coarsening of L12-structured gamma-prime precipitates.
Coarsened L12 precipitates interfere with or pin mobile grain boundaries, producing a serrated grain-boundary morphology.
Serrated grain boundaries distribute strain more evenly than straight grain boundaries.
More even strain distribution mitigates local strain concentration at grain boundaries.
Serrated grain boundaries reduce intergranular void nucleation.
Serrated grain boundaries delay intergranular crack propagation.
The relevant operating condition is continuous creep loading at approximately 650°C under constant applied stress.
Relative to straight grain boundaries, serrated grain boundaries significantly increase creep rupture life, potentially by at least an order of magnitude.
The heat-treated coating will have a lower steady-state creep strain rate than the untreated baseline.
The heat-treated coating will show a more uniform strain distribution across grain boundaries than the baseline.
Much lower temperatures or cyclic loading may produce less creep-resistance enhancement than sustained loading near 650°C.
Applicability of the mechanism to mixed FCC/BCC high-entropy alloys is uncertain.
Long-term operating environments may cause additional microstructural changes that affect the mechanism.
A controlled comparison between heat-treated serrated-boundary coatings and untreated straight-boundary coatings at 650°C can test the hypothesis.
Failure to improve rupture life, creep rate, or strain uniformity, or observing the same enhancement without serrated boundaries, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis is stated specifically for an FCC/BCC coating, while the uncertainty field says it is not known whether the mechanism applies to mixed FCC/BCC structures.
